Identify sources of drugs through pictures: animal, plant, microbiological, mineral, synthetic, and genetically engineered sources.

Identify plant sources of drugs: Atropa belladonna, Pilocarpus microphyllus, Papaver somniferum (Opium poppy), Erythroxylum coca, Cinchona bark, Digitalis purpurea (Foxglove plant), Rauwolfia serpentina, Ephedra vulgaris, Curare, Catharanthus roseus, Podophyllum, and Nux vomica.
Identify animal sources of drugs: Heparin (Pig/Bovine), Insulin (Cow/Pig), Thyroxin (Sheep/Pig), Estrogen, Progesterone, Testosterone, Vitamin A and D (Cod liver), and Vaccines.
Identify microbiological sources of drugs: Penicillins, Cephalosporins, Tetracyclines, Streptomycin, Streptokinase, and Cyclosporine.
Identify mineral sources of drugs: Iron, Magnesium, Zinc, Copper, Silver nitrate, Arsenic, Gold salts, Bismuth salts, Sulfur, Iodine, and Calcium salts.
Identify recombinant / genetically engineered sources of drugs: Human insulin, Erythropoietin, Growth hormone, and Alteplase.
Identify synthetic sources of drugs: Sulfonamides, Anti-histamines, Benzodiazepines, and Anti-epileptics.

Identify and define active principles of drugs (alkaloids, glycosides, volatile oils, fixed oils) through pictures: Alkaloids (Atropine, Caffeine, Morphine, Nicotine, Quinine, Reserpine, Codeine, Tubocurarine), Glycosides (Digoxin, Senna, Cascara), Volatile oils (Clove oil, Peppermint oil, Coriander oil, Dill oil, Ginger oil), and Fixed oils (Coconut oil, Mustard oil, Olive oil, Castor oil, Cod liver oil).
Identify different dosage forms of drugs along with examples: Tablet, Capsule, Syrup, Suspension, Inhaler, Injection, Infusion, Ointment, Cream, Lotion, Lozenges, Suppository, and Enema.
Identify the types of transmembrane receptors on a diagram and give examples.
Describe the changing concepts and new philosophy of health.
Explain responsibility for health in the concept of health.

learningObjectives.objective: F-CM-002. Positive Health Dimensions, Health Determinants
detailedTopics: Explain dimensions and determinants of health and their role in achieving positive health.
Discuss the concept of health and wellbeing in positive health dimensions and health determinants.
Describe the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) and Human Development Index (HDI) as health determinants.
Describe the importance of health indicators.
Classify health indicators.
Define morbidity and mortality as health indicators.
Describe disability indicators as health indicators.
Compare health indicators among countries.
Conceptualize disease causation and the natural history of disease.
Explain germ theory and multifactorial causation of disease.
Describe the Epidemiological Triad of disease causation.
Discuss the Web of disease causation.
Describe the Gradient of infection in disease causation.
Describe principles of disease prevention and control on prevalent diseases.
Explain the difference between elimination and eradication in disease prevention.
Describe disease surveillance, its types, and cycle in disease prevention.
Explain primary, secondary, and tertiary disease prevention.
Describe five levels of interventions in disease prevention.
Identify the biological basis of human behavior and discuss social behavior.
Describe behavioral processes such as neurobiology of memory, emotions, sleep, learning, motivation, sex, arousal, reward, and punishment.
Identify the burden of mental illness on the person, family, and society in psychological disorders.
Describe intellectual disability, mental disorders, and personality disorders.
Identify the role of psychosocial factors in various illnesses (psychology and disease).
Describe psychosocial aspects of various system diseases such as cardiovascular system (CVS), central nervous system (CNS), gastrointestinal tract (GIT), respiratory, renal, endocrine, and cancer.
Identify the behavioral factors associated with pharmacological treatment of diseases.
Discuss the health belief model, treatment compliance and its psychosocial factors, and social factors in drug prescription and drug resistance.
Identify the rehabilitation work for patients on dialysis and with any kind of physical disability in palliative care.
Discuss the palliative care requirements in chronic debilitating conditions like diabetes, multi-infarct dementia, chronic renal disease, and limb amputation.
Identify the various physiological effects of stress.
Explain the Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) response to stress.
Describe behavioral manifestations of stress, and stress-related multiple sclerosis and autoimmune diseases.
Discuss telomeres and telomerase and their clinical significance in the process of aging.
Identify and describe the components of the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue and their function.
Describe the location, coverings, and relations of the spleen as a hematopoietic and lymphoid organ.
Describe the origin, course, branches, and distribution of the splenic artery.
Describe the venous drainage of the spleen, portal vein formation, tributaries, and area of drainage.
Describe the location and relations of the thymus and age-related changes in the thymus.
Describe the intrauterine developmental anatomy of the spleen.

learningObjectives.objective: HL-A-003. Histological features of lymph node, spleen & thymus
detailedTopics: Describe the light microscopic histological features of the spleen, thymus, lymph nodes, tonsils, and Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) including the appendix.
Define, classify, and explain anemia on the basis of morphology and cause.
Discuss the effects of anemia on the body.
Define polycythemia.
Explain the types of polycythemias.
Discuss the effects of polycythemia on the body.
Define hemostasis.
Describe the mechanisms by which hemostasis is secured.
Discuss the characteristics and functions of platelets.
Explain the mechanism of formation of a platelet plug by platelets.
Enlist the clotting (coagulation) factors in blood.
Explain the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and formation of fibrin fibers by coagulation factors.
Explain the intrinsic and extrinsic clotting pathways of coagulation factors.
Name and explain the mechanism of anticoagulants used in the laboratory.
Explain the factors that prevent intravascular coagulation.
Explain the role of calcium ions in intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways.
Enlist the vitamin K-dependent clotting (coagulation) factors.
Explain the prothrombin time, International Normalized Ratio (INR), and its clinical significance in coagulation.
Enlist and explain the conditions that cause excessive bleeding in coagulation disorders.
Define thrombocytopenia as a coagulation disorder.
Enlist the causes and consequences of thrombocytopenia.
Define immunity.
Classify immunity.
Explain humoral immunity.
Explain innate immunity.
Elaborate cell-mediated immunity.
Describe the structure of antigen and immunoglobulin in immunity.
Describe the role of Helper T-cells in cell-mediated immunity.
Enlist the types of immunoglobulins along with their functions in immunity.
Explain the role of memory cells in enhancing antibody response (secondary immune response).
Describe the mechanism of action of antibodies in immunity.
Elaborate the complement system in immunity.
Elaborate immune tolerance.
Explain the process of clone selection during T-cell processing in immune tolerance.
Discuss the failure of immune tolerance mechanisms.
Discuss immunization.
Define passive immunity in relation to immunization.
Explain the features and physiological basis of delayed reaction allergy.
Explain the features and physiological basis of atopic allergy.
Explain the features and physiological basis of anaphylaxis, urticaria, and hay fever.
Discuss the pathophysiology, features, and treatment of ABO and Rh blood group incompatibility.
Enlist the changes that take place in stored blood.
Discuss the features and complications of mismatched blood transfusion reactions.
Describe the hazards of blood transfusion.
Elaborate the transplantation of tissues and organs in relation to immune and transfusion compatibility.
Explain the process of tissue typing for transplantation of tissues.
Explain the prevention of graft rejection in transplantation of tissues by suppressing the immune system.
Interpret the report of Red Blood Cell Count, Hemoglobin concentration, Hematocrit, and RBC Indices by Automated Cell Counter in jaundice, anemias, and homeostasis.
Interpret the report of Total Leucocyte Count, Differential Leucocyte Count, and Platelet Count by Automated Cell Counter in blood disorders and homeostasis.
Determine bleeding time.
Determine clotting time.

learningObjectives.objective: HL-B-001. Hemoglobin and its types/ RBCs
detailedTopics: Explain the steps of synthesis of heme for hemoglobin.
Interpret porphyrias on the basis of signs, symptoms, and data.
Discuss the biochemical role and types of hemoglobin.
Differentiate hemoglobin and myoglobin.
Explain the oxygen dissociation curve of hemoglobin and myoglobin.
Enlist the factors regulating the oxygen dissociation curve of hemoglobin and myoglobin.
Interpret carbon monoxide (CO) toxicity on hemoglobin on the basis of signs and symptoms.
Explain the role of 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG) on hemoglobin in fetal circulation.
Discuss hemoglobinopathies and their biochemical and genetic basis with special emphasis on sickle cell anemia, thalassemia, and methemoglobinemia.
Discuss hypochromic microcytic, normochromic microcytic, normochromic normocytic, and macrocytic (megaloblastic) anemias on the basis of signs, symptoms, and laboratory data.
Explain iron metabolism with its mechanism of absorption and factors affecting iron absorption.
Interpret iron deficiency anemia on the basis of given data and microscopic findings.
Interpret folic acid and cobalamin in relation to anemias on given data and microscopic findings.
Discuss the biochemical role of pyridoxine and vitamins C and K in microcytic anemia and iron metabolism.
Discuss the degradation of heme in macrophages of the reticuloendothelial system.
Describe the formation of bile pigments from heme degradation, their types, and transport.
Discuss the fate of bilirubin formed from heme degradation.
Discuss hyperbilirubinemias and their biochemical basis.
Differentiate types of jaundice in hyperbilirubinemia on the basis of signs/symptoms and data.
Evaluate the genetic basis of jaundice and hyperbilirubinemia on the basis of lab investigations.

Estimate serum Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) level in jaundice and anemias.
Estimate serum Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) level in jaundice and anemias.
Describe the oral and parenteral iron preparations used in anemia, including their pharmacokinetics, uses, adverse effects, and iron antidotes.
Describe Vitamin B12 preparations used in the treatment of anemia.

learningObjectives.objective: HL-Pa-001. Blood Cells, Platelets and Blood Group
detailedTopics: Define hematopoietic growth factors, their names, mechanisms of action, uses, and adverse effects in relation to blood cells.

learningObjectives.objective: HL-BhS-02. Personal, Psychosocial and vocational issues
detailedTopics: Identify and deal with the various personal, psychosocial, and vocational issues of hematopoietic system disorders (such as Sickle Cell Disease, Hemophilia, and Conditions of the Blood) on the individual, family, and society.
